title: write 4 bytes into the allocator's 16-byte alignment slack (offset 28 of a 24-byte request)
object: a, 24 bytes requested, 32 bytes occupied under any 16-byte-aligned allocator
neighbour: b, which starts at offset 32: the defect never reaches it
control: writes a[23], the last byte of the request

asan.why: The dividing line of this case: ASan remembers the REQUEST (24) and poisons 24..31, so it reports on malloc and on an annotated arena that unpoisons exactly n.

valgrind.why: VALGRIND_MEMPOOL_ALLOC is given n, not the rounded size, so the slack stays NOACCESS.

hwasan.why: Short granules again: the tail of the granule carries the 24. HWASan has no public custom-allocator interface, so the annotated columns are UNSUPPORTED, not MISSED (C3.4).

ubsan.why: -fsanitize=bounds needs a statically known array bound; a pointer out of an allocator has none. The row is kept so the report can say UBSan is not a heap tool rather than leaving it out.

lowfat.why: Offset 28 is inside the 32-byte size class, so LowFat is in bounds by construction. This is the case that separates request-granular tools from block-granular ones.

status: written, smoke-run on malloc, arena and freelist; server run pending (A5)
